summary: The web search backend is now an operator choice: `[search] provider = "tavily" | "exa"`. Exa joins Tavily as a second adapter behind the existing SearchProvider port, so `web_search`/`web_fetch` are unchanged.
details: DEC-157. DEC-73 built `SearchProvider` as a port precisely so 'another backend plugs in with no tool change'; `ExaSearchProvider` is that backend. `web_search`/`web_fetch`, their identifier/coordinate egress screen, their budgets and their source tier are untouched — the composition root branches once and everything downstream is handed a SearchProvider it cannot identify.

Exa uses `POST /search` (ranked results with page text in one call) and `POST /contents` (one page), the same two-endpoint split Tavily's `/search` + `/extract` has. The no-SSRF argument carries over unchanged: Exa crawls from Exa's servers, never Nora's, so a model-invented `http://127.0.0.1:18080` still reaches nothing of hers.

`[search]` is reshaped so a third backend costs one sub-table: provider-NEUTRAL knobs (`provider`, `max_results`, `content_max_chars`, `extract_max_chars`, `timeout_seconds`) stay on `[search]`, and each vendor's own endpoints, key name and mode vocabulary move to `[search.tavily]` / `[search.exa]`. The clamps stay neutral on purpose — they bound what re-enters the model's input on every subsequent call, so switching provider must not silently become a token-budget change.

Both adapters are now held to one contract suite (tests/contract/test_search_provider_contract.py), which is what the port's second implementation obliges. The fake speaks each vendor's REAL envelope — Tavily signals a dead link with `failed_results`, Exa with an empty `results` plus an error in `statuses` — so the suite proves two different wire shapes reduce to the same R-27 three states rather than proving something about one shared fake.
limitations: Choosing `provider = "exa"` GIVES UP the relevance floor. Tavily scores every result and `min_score` drops measured junk (0.02-0.05 on opaque-ID and current-state queries, 2026-08-31); Exa deprecated `score` out of auto search and its current result schema carries none, so there is nothing for a floor to read and none is offered. Exa's own ranking is the filter.

Exa's `type` defaults to "auto". The three `deep*` modes run multi-step research with synthesis and routinely outrun `[search] timeout_seconds`, which is sized for one round trip on the reply path — raise it deliberately before selecting one, or every call answers `unavailable`.

Exa's structured extras (`summary`, `highlights`, `subpages`, links and media) are NOT surfaced. Reading them would change what the tools return and what a turn costs, which is a capability decision rather than an adapter one; tracked separately.
Live smoke against the real Exa API has not been run — the adapter is asserted offline against a fake built to the documented envelopes.
